proposed_claim: The relative Fake–Real observed-post gap differs across main contexts.
evidence_limiting: Dataset/context and labels confounded; dependence/coverage limits
allowed_strength: Observational contrast with saved cluster-percentile interval
recommended_wording: The standardized Fake/Real observed-post ratio is lower in CoAID than FakeHealth, indicating a larger relative Fake disadvantage in the CoAID dataset context.

proposed_claim: CoAID is easier to classify within context than FakeHealth.
evidence_limiting: Selected cohorts, source composition and label schemes differ
recommended_wording: Both LR and Linear SVM achieve substantially higher within-context macro F1 in CoAID than FakeHealth.
prohibited_overstatement: COVID misinformation is inherently easier to detect.

proposed_claim: Cross-context text associations have limited portability.
evidence_limiting: Matched target rows improve comparability but source populations and labels differ
recommended_wording: Both classical classifiers show substantial macro-F1 degradation when trained in the other dataset context.
prohibited_overstatement: All misinformation detectors fail outside their training domain.

proposed_claim: Signed lexical coefficients align weakly across datasets.
evidence_limiting: Coefficients conditional on distinct vocabularies/IDF/regularization; no causal decomposition
recommended_wording: Shared-unigram LR coefficients are approximately uncorrelated, and sign reversals remain common among highly ranked shared terms.
prohibited_overstatement: Individual words are universal misinformation cues or causal signaling words.

proposed_claim: Title-only text does not consistently rescue transfer.
evidence_limiting: Small macro-F1 gains coexist with lower ranking scores; training cohorts/configurations differ
recommended_wording: Title-only transfer shows small macro-F1 gains but poorer ROC-AUC in both directions, providing no consistent rescue.
prohibited_overstatement: Removing article bodies never improves any metric, or isolates the effect of length.

proposed_claim: FakeHealth retains modest association under unseen publishers.
evidence_limiting: Publisher proxies incomplete; outer CV not paired with original holdout; no CoAID publisher test
recommended_wording: FakeHealth retains modest predictive signal across unseen publisher families, although performance is lower than the resource-grouped baseline.
prohibited_overstatement: Publisher confounding has been eliminated or cannot explain CoAID performance.

proposed_claim: Explicit source masking leaves residual signal.
evidence_limiting: Label-blind mask uses evaluation metadata; style/topic and other identifiers can remain
recommended_wording: Similar pooled natural and masked publisher-held-out macro F1 suggests known explicit identifiers alone do not account for the surviving FakeHealth signal.
prohibited_overstatement: Source-independent linguistic misinformation detection is established.

proposed_claim: Primary DistilRoBERTa does not consistently improve cross-context transfer.
evidence_limiting: Single-seed primary; unequal token information; macro F1 and ranking disagree
recommended_wording: The primary transformer offers no consistent transfer benefit: a modest macro-F1 gain in one direction coexists with lower ROC-AUC and AP in both directions.
prohibited_overstatement: Transformers always underperform linear models on every metric.

proposed_claim: Transformer budget effects are seed- and metric-sensitive.
evidence_limiting: Limited seeds; only FakeHealth-to-CoAID; threshold/ranking effects differ
allowed_strength: Paired descriptive variability; no inferential claim
recommended_wording: The shorter cap improves macro F1 across tested seeds, but ROC-AUC and AP gains occur only for the original seed; the joint improvement is not stable.
prohibited_overstatement: Shorter source text consistently improves cross-context representation or all budget effects reverse.

proposed_claim: COVID-focused source associations transfer better to independent COVID NEWS.
evidence_limiting: High Fake prevalence; modest threshold performance; source/label/genre differences
allowed_strength: Descriptive external validation; no statistical winner
recommended_wording: Both LR and SVM show greater CoAID-source than FakeHealth-source portability to independent COVID-Rumor NEWS, especially in ROC-AUC.
prohibited_overstatement: A causal sensitive-period effect or universal COVID misinformation vocabulary has been identified.

proposed_claim: External differences are not explained by completely empty representations.
evidence_limiting: Nonzero vectors and higher coverage do not guarantee semantic alignment
recommended_wording: No clean target row has zero TF-IDF features; CoAID has somewhat higher token coverage, which may contribute to its transfer advantage.
prohibited_overstatement: Vocabulary coverage fully explains or rules out representation-related transfer failure.

proposed_claim: Engagement and linguistic findings support a context-dependent interpretation.
evidence_limiting: No causal identification, mediation or item-level text–engagement linkage tested
recommended_wording: Observed Fake/Real engagement contrasts and the portability of learned linguistic associations vary across dataset contexts; independent COVID validation is consistent with greater portability within COVID-focused environments.
prohibited_overstatement: Lexical changes caused the engagement contrast, or COVID caused either pattern.
